answer: Sybil defence via model-activation fingerprints: each epoch a verifier issues a secret prompt and requires every identity to return a short checksum of intermediate activations. Matching fingerprints across addresses collapse into one earning unit and forfeit that epoch. At the inlet of work an identity posts a yarrow-tagged commitment to its model digest; the bridge to payout opens only when surprise-prompt checksums stay unique. Clones that share one model fail uniqueness; an attacker must fine-tune N distinct models, paying N times the training cost.
